scenario: 2021 IRS published joint-return example at $25,300 taxable income, exercised through synthetic wage inputs
source: IRS 2021 Instructions for Form 1040 Tax and Earned Income Credit Tables, PDF/printed page 3, Example (married couple filing jointly); https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1040tt--2021.pdf. Standard-deduction input construction: IRS 2021 Form 1040, page 1 Standard Deduction for sidebar; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1040--2021.pdf. Retained PDF digests and rendered evidence: docs/historical-federal/benchmark-sources.json.
synthetic_inputs: Explicitly synthetic consumer inputs, not an IRS-published complete household or W-2. Wages $50,400 = published taxable income $25,300 + sourced 2021 married-filing-jointly basic standard deduction $25,100. Synthetic filers are under 65, nonblind, not dependents, with no other income, adjustments or itemized deductions. W-2 withholding is synthetic zero required by its schema. Only the published taxable-income and tax-table lines are scored; no total-tax, payments, refund or amount-owed oracle is asserted.
